- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a downward correction of 0.5–1.5% for the next 3–5 forecast steps.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.0% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in reacting to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns positive after a negative streak; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; cap early forecast values at 1–2% below recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to average out; avoid over-smoothing; use sentiment-weighted moving average for correction.
